name: AI Content Translator
description: Translate content entities, taxonomy terms and interface strings into a site's languages using an OpenAI-compatible API, while always preserving human translations.
project_description: AI Content Translator translates content entities (recursing into referenced Paragraphs), taxonomy terms and interface (Twig) strings into a site's languages using any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API — OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or a local server such as Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM — while always preserving human translations. It is deliberately small and self-hosted: set an endpoint, model, token and prompt template, then translate from the UI. Translations it generates are fingerprinted in a key-value store, so a translation a person authors or edits is never overwritten by a normal run; regenerating anything existing requires an explicit overwrite toggle on the bulk form. Every enabled language except the site default is automatically a target — no per-site language configuration. There are three UI entry points: a per-node "Translate with AI" box on the node form, a "Translate (AI)" column on each node's Translations tab, and a bulk "Run translations" admin page for content types, vocabularies and interface strings; long runs use the Batch API for a progress bar. The prompt is a single configurable template with an @language token plus an optional per-language glossary of preferred terms, and optional model parameters (reasoning_effort, verbosity, temperature) are sent only when set so it works across model families. The API token is stored in State (not exported with configuration) and a settings.php value takes precedence for production. Source text is sent to the endpoint you configure, so choose one whose data-handling terms suit your content or run a local model.
